title: KV cache tile orchestration and fragmentation-mitigation protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: As continuous batching and variable sequence lengths increase, GPU-resident KV cache exhibits unpredictable fragmentation which raises eviction churn and reduces effective cache capacity. Goal: Introduce a tile-based KV allocation layer that (1) aligns allocations to GPU memory tiling/paging characteristics, (2) supports eviction-friendly packing (hot-contiguous placement), (3) enables transient spillback to pinned CPU memory during spikes, and (4) provides low-latency background rebalancing that is safe during streaming/continuous-batching workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads
Prototype implemented behind feature flag that maps KV allocations into fixed-size tiles
Benchmarked end-to-end: <=5% P50 generation latency regression at target throughput and >=10% reduction in eviction churn on 1B-token replay workload
Fragmentation metric (defined as unusable gaps / total cache) reduces by >=30% in steady-state workloads vs baseline
Automatic spillback to pinned CPU memory tested for graceful degradation with clear metrics and fallbacks
Telemetry added: tile occupancy heatmap, fragmentation ratio, eviction-churn, spillback events, and background-rebalance latency
design_notes: Tile size selection: default 256KB tile (~fits common KV stripe sizes). Experiment matrix will sweep {64KB,128KB,256KB,512KB} against model families and sequence-length distributions.

Placement heuristic: allocate new KV entries into tiles with contiguous free slots using a first-fit-with-locality policy. Promote tiles tagged as hot to ‘pinned-hot’ pool to avoid mid-request relocation.
Eviction-friendly packing: when freeing slots create a compacting hint rather than immediate defragmentation; background rebalancer will prioritize merging adjacent low-occupancy tiles.
Spillback strategy: overflow writes go to an LRU-ordered pinned CPU page cache with explicit async prefetch back to GPU when tile becomes hot. Policy is conservative to avoid increased tail latency.

Continuous batching consideration: rebalancer is rate-limited and only runs when global batch concurrency < threshold; it performs small, bounded moves (single-tile swaps) to avoid long blocking operations.
Hardware awareness: schedule tile packing to avoid GPU kernel contention (run during low-SM usage windows) and favor unified-memory-aware transfers where supported to reduce copies.
Observability: add per-tile attributes to KV telemetry (last-accessed, occupancy, lifetime, last-move-id) for offline analysis and online rules.
Compatibility: feature should be toggleable per-deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) and per-model to allow staged rollouts.
Failure modes: if rebalancer OOM or crashes, fallback to simple best-effort eviction; ensure routes exist for manual disable and safe drain of moves.
Security: all control-plane ops guarded by existing rollout permissions; no new surface for customer data exfiltration (moves are within same host memory or trusted CPU pin memory).
progress_updates: 2026-01-18: Spike completed — micro-benchmark that measures tile occupancy and simple first-fit allocation. Observed fragmentation pattern correlates strongly with skewed sequence-length workloads.
2026-01-25: Prototype allocator implemented in runtime branch feature/kv-tile — basic tile metadata and allocation API plumbed through request path. Unit tests added.
2026-01-29: Integration smoke tests run on p3-like infra; discovered high-copy overhead when moving tiles back from pinned CPU — need to use async DMA or unified memory where possible.

2026-02-02: Added conservative spillback design: writes spill to pinned CPU memory and prefetch async when tile crosses hot threshold. Initial synthetic tests show reduced immediate OOMs at cost of ~2-3% throughput.

2026-02-07: Telemetry hooks added for tile heatmap and eviction-churn. Dashboard PR opened (link below). Preparing benchmark run against continuous-batching dispatcher with realistic token length distribution.

2026-02-09: Mid-sprint review: runtime and infra leads approved proceeding to extended benchmark. Next: run cluster-scale experiments, tune tile-size heuristics, and draft rollout plan for dedicated-beta customers.
review_feedback: Runtime lead (Sofia Ramirez): prefer conservative default tile size and an operator-visible knob to control rebalancer aggressiveness.
Infra (Jonah Kim): ensure background rebalancer respects cgroup/GPU-isolation to avoid noisy-neighbor interference in Dedicated.
PM (Leah Nguyen): call out migration plan for Dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs — provide canary gating and rollback metrics.
Design (Maya Chen): add UX for visualizing tile heatmap in Console; recommend sampling mode to avoid telemetry cost overhead.
